[Illustration: Frontispiece portrait]

PLATE I.

THOMAS KELLY, LONDON.

[Transcriber's Note: Spelling has been kept as printed.]

THE ENGLISH PHYSICIAN ENLARGED.

WITH THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE MEDICINES MADE OF ENGLISH HERBS.

[1]

ALEHOOF, OR GROUND-IVY.

_Descript._] This well-known herb creeps upon the ground, and
sends forth little branches that take root[2] wherever they
touch the earth. The leaves are round and soft, with scalloped
edges, and the flowers are small and blue.

_Place._] It grows commonly under hedges and by the sides of
ditches in shady places.

_Time._] They flower in April, and abide green until winter.

_Government and virtues._] It is under the dominion of Venus, and
therefore a herb of gentle nature. It is good to tune the lungs
and ease a troublesome cough. Boiled in wine it is held to
cleanse old sores. Take it with honey, and it comforts the
stomach.

ASPARAGUS, SPARAGUS, OR
SPERAGE.

_Descript._] The garden kind rises up with tender green shoots,
which in time grow into tall feathery stalks.

[2]

_Place._] It is sown in gardens, and grows wild upon the sea
coasts in many parts of the kingdom.

_Government and virtues._] It is governed by the Moon. The roots
boiled in wine and drunk are said to open the stopping of the
passages, and to help those that are troubled with the stone.

BALM.

_Descript._] The common balm has square stalks, with broad
wrinkled leaves that smell of lemon.

_Government and virtues._] It is an herb of Jupiter, and under
Cancer. It causes the heart to be merry, and drives away
melancholy and sadness. The juice, mingled with honey, is
a famous cordial.

PLATE II.

THOMAS KELLY, LONDON.

WATER BETONY.

_Descript._] It grows with a square stalk, and the leaves are
dark green, and notched about the edges.

_Place._] It grows by the sides of ponds and ditches.

_Government and virtues._] Jupiter claims dominion over it. A
decoction of the leaves is good for outward wounds.
